findings.summary: The verdict compares raw arm means with an f64::EPSILON tolerance. There is no minimum effect size or noise allowance, so a tiny difference from one run per arm counts as Better or Worse.
findings.evidence: `if (c - b).abs() < f64::EPSILON { NoDifference }` is in effect an exact-equality test. A sounder rule would declare Better or Worse only when the difference exceeds a stated threshold or the spread of the runs. This is acceptable now because the module is not wired into runs, but it should be fixed before it decides anything real.

findings.summary: A NaN metric value is not refused and produces a direction-dependent verdict.
findings.evidence: If either mean is NaN, then (c-b).abs() < EPSILON is false and c < b is false. The result is Worse under LowerIsBetter and Better under HigherIsBetter. validate() could refuse non-finite values instead.

summary: The change adds crates/athena-core/src/method_experiment.rs. It defines a bounded baseline-versus-candidate experiment that is refused when the method is empty, an arm is missing or the bound is zero, stopped when it spends more runs than its bound, and otherwise judged Better, Worse or NoDifference. The module is declared in lib.rs. OLY-9-05 in docs/spec.toml now names it as the mechanism, with owner Athena and the measure `cargo test -p athena-core method_experiment; status: not shown`, the same form as OLY-9-04. The changelog entry was added too. I ran the 5 targeted tests and they pass. They cover every refusal, the Stopped case and all three verdicts, and each one asserts on compare(). Athena's recorded CI checks (fmt, clippy, full test suite) passed. All four changed files are on the deliverables list. Two minor soundness notes, neither blocking: the verdict has no noise threshold and treats any non-equal mean as a real difference, and NaN values are not refused. Verdict: pass.
